title: Leaders Who Lack Courage Allow Bad Ideas to Prosper
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece reframes leadership courage away from tough personnel calls and toward a less visible task: killing bad ideas before they gain traction. It argues that exceptional leaders spend more effort blocking flawed proposals than championing good ones, since a single bad decision can undo many good ones. The article acknowledges the discomfort of disappointing team members who've invested in an idea, but insists this gatekeeping role is essential and requires real courage. It closes by praising leaders willing to say 'no' far more often than 'yes.'
points: Leadership courage is reframed around preventing bad ideas rather than just making tough personnel calls.
A single bad decision can wipe out the gains of many good ones.
Disappointing invested team members by rejecting their ideas is an ongoing, uncomfortable part of the job.
The best leaders actively look for poor decisions that have quietly taken hold and dismantle them.
Courageous leaders say 'no' far more often than they say 'yes.'
quotes: Exceptional leaders don’t make nearly as many good decisions as they do preventing bad ones from gaining traction.
The best leaders know that several good decisions can easily be wiped out by one bad one.
Taking away the oxygen a bad proposal needs to gain a foothold within the team requires the courage to hold a strong view and stick to it.
The best leaders even sniff around looking for poor decisions that have taken hold without much discussion.
Courageous leaders say “No” much more often than they say “Yes.
